fixes.explanation: Baked just right on the jewelry, baker! The men and women bring “…brooches and earrings, rings and necklaces, and all kinds of gold jewelry.” (Exodus 35:22). Rings, necklaces, earrings, brooches. Gold off their own fingers and necks, and they hand it over as a wave offering to the LORD. I can't even give up the last cookie crumb without a speech, and these folks are taking off their rings.

Cups and bowls, friend? Close, but this verse is a jewelry box, not a kitchen cabinet. The people bring “…brooches and earrings, rings and necklaces, and all kinds of gold jewelry.” (Exodus 35:22). That's gold you wear, not gold you eat from. I would have loved a gold mixing bowl, though.

Crowns and shields sound mighty, but that's not on the list. The verse says “…brooches and earrings, rings and necklaces, and all kinds of gold jewelry.” (Exodus 35:22). The men and women bring jewelry, from earrings to necklaces. Fancy, yes, but it's the kind you wear, not the kind you wear into battle.

Gathering tribal leaders isn't what the text says, friend. The craftsmen “left their work and said to Moses…” (Exodus 36:4-5). Their report is: “The people are bringing more than enough for doing the work the LORD has commanded us to do.” (Exodus 36:5). They bring it straight to Moses, and I bet they were grinning.

problems.problem: The explanation is flat and generic. It repeats the answer and the list without a distinctive Papa Dorin moment.
The drawer joke doesn't follow: living in a drawer doesn't explain why he would recognize a cabinet.
The text doesn't say nobody came with armor. It lists the jewelry they brought.
The text doesn't say no meeting was called. It says the craftsmen left their work and spoke to Moses.
